Basin and permanent class cores¶

This notebook reconstructs the spatial eligibility mask from the five thematic windows and the basin geometry. It compares every cell with the archived mask and spatial index. Extract the reference and offline-input archives before running it.

os.environ['RBC_OUTPUT']=str(WORK)

Define eligible positions¶

A position must retain the same TerraClass class in 2016, 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024. The 3×3 erosion keeps positions whose eight neighbours also satisfy permanence. Nearest-neighbour reprojection transfers this mask to the 10 m Brazil Data Cube (BDC) grid; the cell centre determines whether a position belongs to the basin.

The basin intersects tiles 029010 and 030010. Their adjacent cells are processed together for each class and date. The basin area is 459.97 km² in the Albers equal-area projection; the original vector attribute is 463.52 km².

Check the mask and map¶

The comparison should find 1,648,550 eligible cells: 559,153 in primary natural forest vegetation (VNFP), 573,001 in secondary natural forest vegetation (VNFS), and 516,396 in silviculture (SIL). Figure 1 shows these cores and the positions selected across dates. Marker frequency counts returns to a position, including returns on non-consecutive dates.
